newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says guerrilla killed in Israel raid.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says guerrilla killed in Israel raid.

text.p: Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah said on Friday one of its guerrillas was killed in an overnight Israeli air raid on southern Lebanon.
In a statement sent to an international news agency, it said 25-year-old Youssef Ismail Mahdi "was martyred while fighting against an attempted raid by enemy helicopters".
Israel said earlier on Friday its forces killed at least one Hizbollah guerrilla during a clash in its south Lebanon occupation zone on Thursday.

"An Israeli army force on patrol last night on the slopes of Jabal Safi in the eastern sector of the security zone in South Lebanon hit a Hizbollah force, killing at least one terrorist and destroying their vehicle," the army said in a statement.
It said no Israeli soldiers were hurt in the incident.
Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas are fighting to oust Israeli troops and their local militia allies from a 15-km (nine miles)-wide border zone they hold in south Lebanon.

Israel has held a border strip uninterruptedly since its first invasion of Lebanon in 1978. It set the current boundaries of the zone in 1985 after withdrawing the bulk of its forces following a second invasion in 1982.
Security sources in Lebanon said on Thursday night that one guerrilla was wounded when two Israeli helicopters fired five rockets at suspected Hizbollah targets in south Lebanon.
Hizbollah had said its guerrillas fired machineguns and rocket-propelled grenades at Israeli soldiers trying to infiltrate outside the zone.
There was no immediate confirmation of the Hizbollah attack from pro-Israeli militia sources inside the occupation zone.
